corolla.name: Corolla
corolla.tagline: Big houses, wide beaches, and the road runs out here.
corolla.access: The paved road ends at the north end of Corolla — everything beyond (Carova) is 4WD beach driving only. The Currituck Beach Lighthouse is here and climbable in season.

ocean_sands_q.name: Corolla
ocean_sands_q.tagline: Big houses, wide beaches, and the road runs out here.
ocean_sands_q.access: The paved road ends at the north end of Corolla — everything beyond (Carova) is 4WD beach driving only. The Currituck Beach Lighthouse is here and climbable in season.

duck.name: Duck
duck.tagline: The one OBX town you can actually walk.
duck.access: Duck's town center is genuinely walkable — a soundfront boardwalk connects shops and restaurants, which is rare on the Outer Banks.

southern_shores.name: Southern Shores
southern_shores.tagline: The quiet one — residential by design, and it shows.
best_for: Repeat visitors who've outgrown the crowds
Central location without the commercial strip
southern_shores.access: Southern Shores sits at the foot of the Wright Memorial Bridge — it's the first town you reach coming onto the northern beaches, which makes changeover-day arrivals easier than the towns farther north.

kitty_hawk.name: Kitty Hawk
kitty_hawk.tagline: Central, practical, and the best value on the northern beaches.
best_for: A central base for exploring the whole OBX
kitty_hawk.access: The Wright brothers' first flight is named for Kitty Hawk because of the weather station that handled their telegrams — the actual flight site and memorial are just south in what's now Kill Devil Hills.

carova.name: Carova
carova.tagline: No pavement, no shops, wild horses in the yard.
best_for: People who find beach driving part of the fun
carova.access: 4WD is required for all access — there is no paved road into Carova; you drive the beach north from the end of NC-12 in Corolla, and rental agreements assume it.

kill_devil_hills.name: Kill Devil Hills
kill_devil_hills.tagline: Where flight started, and where everything on the OBX is close.
best_for: Families who want restaurants and groceries close
kill_devil_hills.access: The Wright Brothers National Memorial — site of the first powered flight in 1903 — sits in the middle of town, and the monument hill is visible from much of the bypass.

nags_head.name: Nags Head
nags_head.tagline: The classic OBX beach town, from old cottages to big group houses.
best_for: Travelers who want the traditional OBX feel
nags_head.access: Jockey's Ridge State Park protects the tallest natural sand dune system on the East Coast, and it's free to enter and climb.

south_nags_head.name: South Nags Head
south_nags_head.tagline: Nags Head's quiet end — beach houses, few storefronts, open road south.
best_for: Repeat visitors who know what they want
south_nags_head.access: South Nags Head ends at Oregon Inlet, the crossing point to Hatteras Island — day trips down Hatteras start closer here than from anywhere else in the central OBX.

rodanthe.name: Rodanthe
rodanthe.tagline: First stop past the bridge, and it feels like it.
rodanthe.access: The Marc Basnight Bridge over Oregon Inlet is the only road onto Hatteras Island — every drive down starts with that crossing.

waves.name: Waves
waves.tagline: The tri-villages' quiet middle, with wind on the sound side.
waves.access: Waves has no hard boundary with its neighbors — you'll pass through Rodanthe on NC-12 to get here, and Salvo starts before you notice Waves ended.

salvo.name: Salvo
salvo.tagline: Southernmost, smallest, and quietest of the tri-villages.
salvo.access: South of Salvo, NC-12 runs through miles of national seashore with no development until Avon — the emptiest stretch of road on the island.

avon.name: Avon
avon.access: Avon has the only full-size grocery store on this stretch of the island — a real logistical advantage over the tri-villages to the north.

island_creek.name: Avon
island_creek.access: Avon has the only full-size grocery store on this stretch of the island — a real logistical advantage over the tri-villages to the north.

kinnakeet_shores.name: Avon
kinnakeet_shores.access: Avon has the only full-size grocery store on this stretch of the island — a real logistical advantage over the tri-villages to the north.

buxton.name: Buxton
buxton.tagline: The lighthouse, the point, and the best-known surf on the island.
buxton.access: The Cape Hatteras Lighthouse is in Buxton, inside Cape Hatteras National Seashore — the island's most-visited landmark.

frisco.name: Frisco
frisco.tagline: Buxton's quieter neighbor, one village further down.
frisco.access: Frisco puts you within a few miles of both Canadian Hole and the Cape Hatteras Lighthouse — close to the action without being in it.

hatteras_village.name: Hatteras Village
hatteras_village.tagline: The end of the road — literally.
hatteras_village.access: The free NC-operated Hatteras–Ocracoke ferry departs from the village — about a 70-minute crossing, no reservation needed, on a seasonal schedule.

manteo.name: Manteo
manteo.tagline: The Outer Banks town that isn't on the banks.
best_for: Couples and small families who want a real town
A downtown you can walk, a harbor, history within reach
manteo.access: Reached via US-64 across the Virginia Dare Memorial Bridge — a separate approach from the NC-12 beach corridor. Nags Head is roughly a 10-minute drive east.

ocracoke.name: Ocracoke
ocracoke.tagline: The island you can only reach by boat.
best_for: People who want the trip itself to be the point
A real island, a walkable village, beaches with room to spread out
Return visitors who've outgrown the busier towns
ocracoke.access: Free ferry from the south end of Hatteras Island (about 70 minutes), or longer toll ferries from Swan Quarter and Cedar Island on the mainland. Check schedules before you book your arrival day.
